title: Does this order pass?
hook: A checker passes 9, 2, 5 because all three numbers are there.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Apply a stated sorting rule to visible values rather than repeat its wording.

misconception: Any arrangement containing the right values applies ascending order.
objective: Apply a stated sorting rule to visible values rather than repeat its wording.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: A checker passes 9, 2, 5 because all three numbers are there. Under the ascending rule, how many of 9, 2, 5 are already in the right place? Correct option: 0 of 3 (ascending is 2, 5, 9). Exercise values are conventions, not measured learning data.

claims.text: The displayed match count compares the learner’s ordering of 2, 5, 9 with ascending order. The unsorted input stays visible while they work. There is no measured learning or productivity gain.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, apply-not-quote fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three. Application refinement presents new unsorted input 5, 9, 2 and leaves it visible while the learner rearranges the separate attempt row. No Cover control is offered; a real swap is required before checking. Feedback marks which attempt positions match ascending order 2, 5, 9 after Check; the unsorted input remains unchanged. This is a rule-application fixture, not a recall or retention test. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Ascending means smallest to largest: 0.125 < 0.25 < 0.5. The last option only repeats the given order, which passes 'all three are there' but not the rule.

recall.question: Apply the ascending rule to 0.25, 0.5 and 0.125. Which order is correct?
recall.why: Ascending means smallest to largest: 0.125 < 0.25 < 0.5. The last option only repeats the given order, which passes 'all three are there' but not the rule.
